title: Senior Director, AI Strategy and Innovation
description:
Responsibilities
Network AI Strategy and Leadership

• Translate the strategy so it travels: a regional superintendent can repeat it in a sentence, a development officer can put it in front of a funder, and a school leader recognizes it in the guidance they receive.

AI Pilot Leadership and Measurement

• Manage the AI pilot group, setting its priorities and the standard of evidence for AI pilots across the Foundation and regions.

• Design and administer the measurement system for AI pilots: go to regions to assess pilot quality, collect, and analyze evidence, and produce a report on each pilot that states clearly whether the tool is working and for which students.

• Partner with the Schools team, which oversees instructional pilots, and with external researchers to set the comparison design, subgroup breakouts, and data plan before licenses are issued.

• Apply a common evaluation framework to every AI tool under consideration, covering efficacy and alignment to One KIPP anchor metrics; accessibility for multilingual learners, students with IEPs, and students arriving below grade level; bias and equity risk; implementation requirements and total cost of ownership; and student data privacy and security, with the Data and Technology team setting technical, privacy, and security requirements.

AI Recommendations and Partnerships

• Serve as the final recommender on AI vendors, uses, and approaches for both Foundation and regional work, including work led by the Schools team, where the Chief Schools Officer makes the final decision.

• Help Foundation teams use AI more effectively in their own work, keeping the principles for the Foundation's internal AI use and the standard for classroom tools in one coherent position.

Network Coordination Across Regions

• Coordinate AI work across KIPP regions, maintaining a current inventory of tools, cost, funding source, early outcomes, lessons learned, and privacy considerations through regional AI leads and touchpoints such as RAMP, so the Foundation can answer a question about network AI use the week it is asked.

• Advise regions on how tools fit KIPP 's approach and what evidence the network needs to recommend them, respecting regional leaders' authority over their own schools.

• Broker multi-region pilots with a shared challenge, a common evaluation design, and a clear division of labor, so the network learns once instead of many times and reduces duplicate spending.

Funding, Ecosystem, and External Voice

• Build KIPP 's relationships with funders investing in AI in education and, with the Development team, position KIPP to attract the philanthropic dollars and support its priority AI work needs, coordinating regional and national requests so KIPP does not compete with itself.

Quartermaster is building the world's most comprehensive maritime intelligence platform. Our SmartMast™ system transforms commercial and civilian vessels into a persistent, distributed sensing network-combining HD video, AI, radar, RF sensing, and AIS to deliver real-time maritime domain awareness at global scale. With 600+ sensors deployed across 25+ countries and more than 400,000 vessels identified outside of AIS, we are setting a new standard for what ocean surveillance and safety can look like.

We are a startup in build mode: small team, high ownership, fast iteration, and meaningful constraints. We ship quickly, learn in production, and optimize for mission impact over process theater.

The Role

As Regional Field Operations Manager, you will own the deployment and performance of SmartMast™ across your region. Once Launch has opened a market and secured vessel partners, you turn those agreements into units that are installed, activated, and reporting, and you keep them reporting. Success is measured in units installed on schedule, uptime across the regional fleet, and the speed and quality of every install and repair.

You will build and run the regional field operation: technicians, installers, logistics, and spares. You will work hand in hand with the regional Head of Launch and report to Quartermaster's Field Operations leadership in the United States.

What You'll Own

- Deployment: Plan and execute SmartMast™ installations across the region's vessel partners, from vessel survey and scheduling through install, activation, and first data. Hit the deployment targets set with Launch and leadership.

- Fleet uptime: Keep every installed unit online and reporting. Own preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, and unit swaps against clear response-time standards.

- Field team: Recruit, train, and lead regional field technicians and coordinators. Set the bar for install quality, safety, and professionalism aboard vessels.

- Logistics and inventory: Run in-country hardware flow, including receiving, warehousing, spares, staging, and reverse logistics for failed units, within the import framework Launch establishes.

- Vendor and installer management: Direct the local installers, fabricators, and port-side vendors that Launch onboards. Schedule their work, audit quality, and escalate or replace underperformers.

- Vessel and port coordination: Work with fleet operations teams, crews, and port staff to get aboard during short windows, around vessel schedules, port calls, and access rules.

- Field data and feedback: Track install, uptime, and repair metrics. Feed hardware and install issues back to engineering, and surface field realities to Launch and leadership.

- Process: Build repeatable install and maintenance procedures, safety practices, and documentation that scale across countries.

What You Need

- Experience: 6+ years in field operations, field service, or technical deployment, including at least 3 years leading field teams. Maritime, offshore, telecoms, or marine electronics strongly preferred.

- Deployment track record: Proven delivery of hardware rollouts across multiple sites or countries, on schedule and to quality standards.

- Hands-on technical depth: Comfort with vessel-installed electronics, including mounting, power, cabling, networking, and RF/antenna work. You can step aboard and troubleshoot alongside your team.

- Logistics instinct: Inventory and spares planning, customs-ready shipping, and getting parts to a vessel during a short port call.

- Safety: Working knowledge of shipboard safety practice and port access procedures in the region.

- Location: Based in the region and ready to travel up to 50% to ports and vessels, sometimes on short notice.

- Autonomy: Comfortable running an operation with leadership several time zones away.

- Language: Fluent professional English, plus the primary working languages of the region's ports and crews.

title: Marketplace Deal Operations Specialist, EMEA
description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale - unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data - securing and protecting private information more effectively - Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role

We’re hiring a Marketplace Deal Operations Analyst to become the hands-on expert in cloud marketplace transactions (AWS, Azure and GCP) for our EMEA business. This role takes the operational detail of lower segment marketplace deals off Deal Desk Analysts and Field sellers, so they can focus on strategy, structuring and higher-value deals. It is a distinct function from Deal Desk Analyst: a specialist execution and process-ownership role for someone who wants to go deep on marketplace mechanics, build genuine subject-matter expertise, and bring order to a high-volume, detail-heavy process.

If you enjoy being the person everyone turns to for the right answer, and you take pride in getting every detail right at speed, this role is for you.

CET business hours (approx. 1:30pm-10:30pm IST in winter, 12:30pm-9:30pm IST in summer)

What You Will Be Doing

•
Executing marketplace transactions at high velocity

• Generate, submit and manage private offers across AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace for EMEA deals

• Own the end-to-end execution of marketplace transactions: validating deal requirements, ensuring documentation accuracy, and processing offers against defined SLAs

• Process amendments, renewals and cancellations

•
Becoming the marketplace expert

• Be the go-to subject-matter expert on operational marketplace processes across all three hyperscalers for the EMEA organization

• Spot process gaps and create clear, repeatable guidance (SOPs, checklists and playbooks) so Field and Deal Desk can self-serve where possible

• Stay current on program and process changes from AWS, Azure and GCP, and turn them into updated internal guidance

•
Supporting Deal Desk and Field

• Provide hands-on administrative support on marketplace transactions to Deal Desk Analysts and EMEA Field sellers

• Resolve ad-hoc operational issues and one-off transaction challenges as they arise

• Act as the first point of contact for “how do I handle this marketplace scenario?” transactional process questions from the field

•
Growing into Deal Desk

• Over time, build working knowledge of broader Deal Desk processes

• Provide ad-hoc deal support to the Deal Desk team when volume or complexity requires it, as a development opportunity rather than a core responsibility

What You Bring

• Direct, hands-on experience with cloud marketplace transactions (AWS, Azure and/or GCP Marketplace) in a B2B SaaS environment

• Experience working in a high-velocity SaaS company

• Sound judgment in nuanced, non-templated scenarios. This is not a pure checklist-following role

• Exceptional attention to detail, with accuracy in documentation and process treated as non-negotiable

• Strong organization and analytical skills, with the ability to manage a high volume of concurrent, detail-heavy transactions without anything slipping

• Comfort with repeatable, high-volume work, and an understanding that transaction volume will fluctuate

• The confidence to ask questions and surface ambiguity rather than guess silently

• Ambition and motivation to provide excellent support to a field sales organization

• Strong written and verbal English communication skills, as you’ll work daily with EMEA Field and Deal Desk

OpenAI’s Compute Strategy & Partnerships team develops the partnerships and transactions that support our long-term ambitions. We’re looking for a Business Development professional to help originate, structure, negotiate, and execute complex strategic partnerships. description:
your mission

About the role

AI didn't kill the SDR role. It killed the average one. The ones who survive - and win - are the ones who figured out how to use AI as a force multiplier rather than a shortcut.
This is not a high-volume, spray-and-pray prospecting role. Timefold sells a technical platform into companies where scheduling, routing, and optimization are commercially important. Good outbound therefore starts with understanding the account, identifying the right trigger, and creating a relevant reason for the right person to speak with us.
You will work closely with Account Executives, Marketing, and Solutions Engineering to create qualified conversations in target accounts. You will focus on software vendors, OEMs, and technically mature organisations with complex planning problems.
The SDR owns the work before the opportunity: account research, outreach, early qualification, and a clean handoff to Sales. The Account Executive owns the opportunity and commercial process once it is qualified.
This role reports to the Head of Sales.
What the role looks like
Build qualified outbound demand

• You dig into target accounts and prioritize them based on ICP fit, relevant use cases, company context, product or open-source adoption signals, and commercial potential - no spray-and-pray here.

• You catch the signals that actually matter: hiring sprees, funding rounds, product launches, tech stack changes, content engagement, or operational complexity that screams "we need this."

• You map accounts like a detective, pinpointing the technical, operational, and executive stakeholders who actually move the deal.

• You run outreach that doesn't feel like outreach - tailored messages across email, phone, LinkedIn, and the communities where our audience actually hangs out.

• You turn conversations into qualified meetings and Sales-accepted leads that AEs are genuinely excited to pick up.

• You keep HubSpot squeaky clean - contacts, activity, source, lead status, and qualification data, all accurate, all the time.

• You share the playbook, openly: what messaging lands, what objections keep popping up, which personas and signals convert, and which account segments are worth chasing.

• You team up with Marketing, trading campaign feedback, outbound insights, and content ideas that actually make prospects lean in.

• You help shape Timefold 's outbound motion as we scale - this isn't a role where you follow a script, it's one where you help write it.

Craft outreach for technical buyers
We are targeting developers, architects, engineering leaders, product leaders, and data teams - that means you'll touch upon genuinely complex planning and optimization problems, not just the buzzwords around them.

• You engage operational and executive stakeholders with messaging tied to business outcomes: service quality, operational efficiency, scheduling complexity, growth, and build-versus-buy decisions.

• You know the difference between a technical evaluator, a champion, an operational stakeholder, and the economic buyer - and you flex your approach accordingly, because one-size-fits-all pitches don't work on people who solve hard problems for a living.

• You treat open-source and community signals as a research starting point, not a shortcut - you validate relevance before ever mistaking interest for intent.

Convert & engagement
Success is not measured only by emails sent or meetings booked.

• Meaningful engagement in target accounts - not just opens and clicks, but real conversations.

• Meetings that actually show up and get accepted by Sales.

• Sales-qualified leads with credible fit, real intent, and a clear next step - no mystery leads.

• Opportunities sourced from the right accounts and segments, not just whoever answered the phone.

• Sharp insight on which messages, personas, and triggers actually convert - so the whole team gets smarter, not just you.
